rounds.proof_sketch: After `cg::reduce(warp, thread_sum, cg::plus<float>())`, all 32 threads in each warp hold the identical `warp_sum` value (cooperative groups reductions broadcast results to all participating threads). Original: thread 0 writes `warp_sum` to `block_sums[meta_group_rank]`. Mutated: threads 1-31 write the same `warp_sum` to `block_sums[meta_group_rank]`. Since all writers write the identical value to the same address, the final memory state is identical regardless of which threads perform the write.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes which threads within a warp write to shared memory: from thread 0 only (`== 0`) to threads 1-31 (`!= 0`). However, this is semantically equivalent because cooperative groups' `cg::reduce` function broadcasts its result to ALL participating threads in the tile. After the warp reduction, every thread in the warp holds the exact same `warp_sum` value. Whether one thread writes this value or 31 threads simultaneously write it to the same memory location, the observable result in `block_sums[warp.meta_group_rank()]` is identical. The `block.sync()` ensures all writes complete before any reads occur. No value pattern can distinguish these two behaviors because the computed values are invariant to which specific thread performs the write.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation is semantically equivalent because cooperative groups reductions broadcast results to all threads. All potential writers have the same value, so the mutation cannot produce different outputs under any input values.
rounds.recommendations: When analyzing mutations involving cooperative groups operations, recognize that `cg::reduce` on a tile broadcasts the result to ALL threads in the tile, not just thread 0. Mutations that change which thread writes a broadcast value are often semantically equivalent and should be classified as equivalent mutants during mutation testing setup.
